newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends pre-Easter trade narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends pre-Easter trade narrowly mixed.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures crawled from session's lows to end on Thursday narrowly mixed in lethargic, pre-Easter holiday dealings, traders said.

Origin selling drove the market into the negative territory in the early afternoon but nearby positions managed to recoup slight gains at the close on end-of-the-year book-squaring and pre-holiday short-covering. March 31 is the end of the financial year for some stores.

The day's volume of 3,197 lots also comprised arbitrage buying against New York as the arabica futures raced higher at the start of the trading. However it pulled back slightly to finish midsession lower on profit-taking.
By the close, London's benchmark May stood $2 higher at $1,632 per tonne after trading between $1,610 and $1,650.

Spot March went off the board at lunchtime without a bang. It expired at $1,623, up $12, on a volume of 52 lots. The March open positions on the contract stood at just 120 lots, down 457, by Wednesday's close.
Long holders of March continued to receive tenders. By Thursday, deliveries reached 17,365 tonnes including re-tenders.
The London market is closed on Friday and Monday for Easter, reopening on Tuesday.
May/May arbitrage widened further to over $1.00 after holding around 90 cents earlier in the week. It stood at $1.12 at 1731 GMT.
The New York market had posted steep gains for two days in a row by Wednesday as speculators continued to buy heavily amid lingering supply woes.

After Wednesday's New York close, the Association of Coffee Producing Countries' secretariat said in a report that the supply prospects in the third quarter of 1997 continued to look tight and could be vulnerable to disruptions.
The London-based group also lowered its estimate for the Central American 1996/97 crop to 15.4 million bags from its previous forecast of 15.8 million.
It only lowered world consumption to 76 million bags on an annualised basis from its previous forecast of 76.5 million.
Technically, analysts said the robusta market now looked capable of holding support at $1,600-$1,500 for now after eroding support at much higher levels.
But the upside potential looked limited.
"Overhead supply dominates and the potential for gains does not look large," Investment Research of Cambridge said on a weekly report. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
